title: Selling Plans Chargeback Timing Multiplier on Administration Fees
content:
A chargeback that arrives soon after a sale costs the seller more in administration fee on a **Selling Plans** chargeback credit. The timing is read from two dates: the date of the most recent chargeback debit on the seller's Northloop Payments ledger, and the billing date of the charged-back order's variable final value fee record.

**Rule.** The chargeback administration fee is multiplied by the quick-chargeback multiplier when the chargeback was debited no more than the quick-chargeback days after the order's variable fee billing date, by the mid-chargeback multiplier when it was debited later but no more than the mid-chargeback days after, and by one when it was debited later still.

The multiplier applies to the administration fee as worked out from the credit before the fee and its rate; the product is then rounded to the nearest cent, and only the rounded amount is compared with the cap.

## Multiplier by days between the two dates (calendar days)

| Chargeback debited after the variable fee billing date | Multiplier on the administration fee |
|---|---|
| 14 days or fewer (the quick-chargeback days) | 1.5 (quick-chargeback multiplier) |
| 15 to 45 days (up to the mid-chargeback days) | 1.25 (mid-chargeback multiplier) |
| 46 days or more | One |

## Both sides of each boundary (variable fee billed on hypothetical 1 March)

| Chargeback debit date | Days after 1 March | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| 15 March | 14 | 1.5 |
| 16 March | 15 | 1.25 |
| 15 April | 45 | 1.25 |
| 16 April | 46 | One |

**Applying it (hypothetical).** A credit before the fee of USD 20.00 at a rate of 20% gives USD 4.00; multiplied by 1.5 it is USD 6.00, and USD 6.00 is then compared with the cap.
